ann_30.text: Through this part, going from 0 to 2 vessels coloured raises a typical patient's predicted risk from about 20% to about 45% (on the training data only).
A thallium result coded 4 raises it from about 20% to about 93% through this part (2 patients; the model has little data on this; on the training data only).

ann_31.text: This part acts on 160 of 242 training patients (66%), all of them patients without chest pain on exercise; 47 of them had heart disease.

For the typical patient it acts on (a 54-year-old man with non-anginal chest pain, 0.4 mm of ST depression and a maximum heart rate of 159 beats per minute), it changes the predicted risk only slightly, which stays at about 1% (on the training data only).

Through it, being a woman lowers a typical patient's predicted risk from about 20% to about 7%, and chest pain brought on by exercise raises it from about 20% to about 27% (on the training data only).
Across the whole model, being a woman clearly lowers the predicted risk more if exercise does not bring on chest pain (from about 20% to below 1%, against about 27% to about 1% with it).

ann_32.text: This part acts on only 15 of 242 training patients (6%), all of them patients with a fixed defect on the thallium scan; 9 of them had heart disease.

For the typical patient it acts on (a 57-year-old man with a fixed thallium defect, 1 vessel coloured, a flat ST segment, 1.5 mm of ST depression and signs of left ventricular hypertrophy), it lowers the predicted risk from above 99% to about 90% (the model has little data on this; on the training data only).
Through it, a fixed defect lowers a typical patient's predicted risk from about 20% to about 1% (15 patients; the model has little data on this; on the training data only).

A fixed defect lowers the predicted risk only if fasting blood sugar is 120 mg/dL or less (from about 20% to about 1%, while it stays at about 3% above 120 mg/dL). The model has little data on this: only 15 training patients (a fixed defect on the thallium scan).
For the typical patient this part acts on, fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL raises the predicted risk through it from about 90% to above 99% (on the training data only).

ann_33.text: This part acts on 70 of 242 training patients (29%), and 50 of them had heart disease.

ann_35.original: Root: logit z = -0.954 + LINEAR CORE + 1.893*vessel_count_linear_boost - 0.452*sex_exang_protective_gate - 0.942*fbs_normal_fixed_defect_gate + 1.108*oldpeak_hinge - 0.154*cp2_constant_offset; prediction = sigmoid(z) (get_formula shows the output node as ReLU, but the evaluator overrides it with sigmoid for binary classification; compute_performance on train, AUC 0.9437 and acc 0.888, matches sigmoid(z)). LINEAR CORE (standardised inputs): +2.065 ca, +1.665 sex:1, -0.070 sex:0, +1.298 slope:2, -0.499 slope:1, +1.075 chol, -0.972 cp:3, -0.916 cp:1, +0.618 cp:4, -0.057 cp:2, -0.667 fbs:1, +0.616 trestbps, +0.461 thal:7, -0.419 thalach, +0.205 age. Inputs restecg:0/1/2, exang:1, slope:3 and thal:3 are disconnected in the phenotype and enter the root with zero effect. summary.text: For a typical patient (a 56-year-old man with no chest pain symptoms and median test results, predicted risk about 20%), the model clearly gives a much lower predicted risk of heart disease with typical angina (below 1%), non-anginal chest pain (about 1%) or atypical angina (about 5%).

Going from 0 to 2 vessels coloured by fluoroscopy raises a typical patient's predicted risk from about 20% to about 99%, and a flat rather than upsloping ST segment at peak exercise raises it to about 90% (on the training data only).

Being a woman lowers the predicted risk, and even more so if exercise does not bring on chest pain: for a typical patient it clearly falls from about 20% to below 1% without chest pain on exercise, and from about 27% to about 1% with it.

A fixed defect on the thallium scan lowers the predicted risk, but only if fasting blood sugar is 120 mg/dL or less: from about 20% to about 1% in that case, while it stays at about 3% with fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL. The model has little data on this: only 15 training patients (a fixed defect on the thallium scan).

Higher cholesterol (193 to 308 mg/dL) raises a typical patient's predicted risk from about 8% to about 53%, and ST depression on exercise adds risk only once it rises above about 1.5 mm, moving it from about 20% to about 61% between 0 and 3.5 mm (on the training data only).

summary.text: For a typical patient, number of vessels coloured by fluoroscopy going from 0 vessels to 2 vessels raises the predicted risk of heart disease from about 20% to about 99% (on the training data only).

For a typical patient, the model gives a higher predicted risk of heart disease if the ST segment is flat at peak exercise (about 90%) than if the ST segment slopes up at peak exercise (about 20%) (on the training data only).
For a typical patient, serum cholesterol going from 193 mg/dL (5.0 mmol/L) to 308 mg/dL (8.0 mmol/L) raises the predicted risk of heart disease from about 8% to about 53% (on the training data only).

Through one part of the model, ST depression on exercise only adds to the predicted risk of heart disease once it rises above about 1.5 mm: for a typical such patient, going from 0.0 mm to 3.5 mm moves it from about 20% to about 61% (on the training data only).

For a typical patient, going from male to female moves the predicted risk of heart disease from about 20% to below 1% if exercise does not bring on chest pain, and from about 27% to about 1% if exercise brings on chest pain.
